question: Did the January 22, 2026 approval give Con Edison the $1,611.6 million first-year electric increase proposed in its February 7, 2025 notice? Give the proposed and approved headline amounts.
answer: No. The proposal notice states $1,611.6 million; the compliance notice states a first-year increase of $234.0 million ($227.6 million exclusive of gross receipts tax).

answer: RY3 funding is planned for engineering, feasibility and exploratory work for obsolete Feeder 99031. The response explicitly schedules no complete feeder replacement in RY3.

1. Referring to page 112 of Exhibit  (EIOP-8), explain why the projected costs go

construction on the new 38R51/38R52 feeders occurring from 2022 to 2024. The feeders 
were originally expected to be energized in 2023, but access and permission issues 
related to routing through the Staten Island landfill resulted in a one-year delay.
